historicalRuling.approvedInterpretation: Counterfactual command abstraction anchored in the RBiH Presidency's 8-9 April 1992 effort to place armed individuals and units under a single TO command.
historicalRuling.historicalDefaultMeaning: Integration-or-refusal policy toward a parallel paramilitary track, not a claim of complete effective control at turn 0.

sensitiveHistoryRuling.reason: The complete existing policy event may be offered earlier without a new atrocity instruction, but always_allow can enable two immediate simulated captures and may never be framed as a benefit, historical parity, or calibration remedy.

conditions.requirement: Treat the turn-0 event as a general command-policy abstraction after identity; add no dated meeting, order, quotation, or claim that the exact three-option decision occurred historically.

Preserve the distinction between an integration-or-refusal policy and uneven effective control; do not imply that all irregular, criminal, or local fighting groups were subordinated at campaign birth.
Keep always_deny as the sole historical default and ask/always_allow as counterfactual; no preselection, hidden Historical-mode inference, or automatic consent.

Move the whole existing event with all three authored options, descriptions, source fields, effects, flags, dimensions, notifications, consequences, receipts, civilian-casualty accounting, and war-crime accounting; no split authority or direct policy write.
Use the two retained turn-1 bot captures only as capability evidence; make no historical capture claim, no all-seven-differences causal claim, and no calibration tuning or adoption claim.
Add no reward, parity, recovery, optimization, territorial-opportunity, military-necessity, score, achievement, or casualty-to-territory framing for always_allow.

Bind the April timing justification to ICTY Hadzihasanovic and Kubura IT-01-47-T paragraphs 312-313 and/or BB1 pages 166-169. Do not use UN A/54/549 paragraph 35 as evidence of Sarajevo's April single-command policy; it concerns the Srebrenica enclave's raids and counter-raids.
Leave event data, headless/no-player behavior, sweep/target/control/scoring logic, thresholds, protected controls, n91-n95, and all telemetry unchanged; any expansion returns to the panel.
Treat this as one independent Historian seat only; implementation requires every other specified review and unanimous section-6 panel approval.

sourceAudit.source: ICTY Hadzihasanovic and Kubura Trial Judgment IT-01-47-T
sourceAudit.finding: On 8 April 1992 the Presidency established the RBiH TO Staff; on 9 April it ordered armed individuals and units to report to TO staffs and come under a single command.
sourceAudit.supports: opening timing for a general command-policy abstraction

sourceAudit.finding: The Presidency's May-July 1992 decrees sought a joint armed structure while effective organization remained incomplete.
The Patriotic League was organized with Presidency/SDA approval before the war and its command entered the state TO structure in April 1992.
sourceAudit.supports: prewar provenance and April integration timing

sourceAudit.finding: Early Sarajevo forces remained heterogeneous and partly autonomous; professionalization and the Caco/Celo crackdown came later.
sourceAudit.supports: no claim of complete turn-0 control

sourceAudit.finding: Describes raids and counter-raids from the Srebrenica enclave and reported abuses during Bosniac expansion.
sourceAudit.supports: not admissible as evidence for Sarajevo's April single-command policy

causalBoundary.proven: Retained evidence shows two immediate turn-1 RBiH bot captures absent from the ordinary player lane.
causalBoundary.notProven: Those captures are historically authentic RBiH paramilitary actions, the timing difference caused all seven January differences, or any calibration floor should change.

preserve: sweep, target, control, capture, and scoring semantics
